tagline: Art Basel, M+, auction records and how to talk about art without bluffing.
why: Hong Kong is Asia's art market capital, home to Art Basel Hong Kong, the M+ museum and major auction houses. Art comes up at gallery openings, dinners and in news about record-breaking sales. You don't need an art history degree; knowing the major movements, famous names, local institutions and some useful vocabulary lets you enjoy and discuss art confidently.

essentials.title: Major movements
essentials.body: Renaissance (Leonardo, Michelangelo), Impressionism (Monet), Post-Impressionism (Van Gogh), Cubism (Picasso), Abstract Expressionism (Pollock, Rothko), Pop Art (Warhol) and Contemporary art.

essentials.title: Contemporary vs modern
essentials.body: Modern art is roughly 1860s to 1970s; contemporary art is from the 1970s to now.

essentials.title: The art market
essentials.body: Galleries sell new work (primary market); auction houses resell it (secondary market). Christie's, Sotheby's and Phillips dominate auctions.

essentials.title: Art fairs
essentials.body: Art Basel (Basel, Miami, Hong Kong, Paris) and Frieze gather galleries from around the world.

essentials.title: Chinese and Asian art
essentials.body: From ancient ceramics and ink painting to modern masters like Zao Wou-Ki and Sanyu and contemporary stars like Ai Weiwei and Yayoi Kusama.

essentials.title: How to look at art
essentials.body: Ask what you notice, how it makes you feel, and what the artist might be saying. There's no wrong reaction.

names.name: M+
names.what: Hong Kong's museum of visual culture in West Kowloon, opened 2021; one of the world's major contemporary museums.

names.name: Hong Kong Palace Museum
names.what: Opened 2022 with treasures from Beijing's Palace Museum.

names.name: Art Basel Hong Kong
names.what: Asia's top art fair, every March.

names.name: Yayoi Kusama
names.what: Japanese artist of polka dots and infinity rooms; M+ held a big retrospective.

names.name: Zao Wou-Ki
names.what: Chinese-French abstract painter whose works fetch huge prices in Hong Kong auctions.

names.name: Andy Warhol
names.what: Pop Art icon of soup cans and Marilyns.

names.name: Jean-Michel Basquiat
names.what: Neo-expressionist painter; his works sell for over $100 million.

names.name: Tsang Tsou-choi
names.what: 'The King of Kowloon', whose calligraphy graffiti became celebrated art.

names.name: Christie's / Sotheby's / Phillips
names.what: The big auction houses, all with major Hong Kong bases.

names.name: Gagosian / Hauser & Wirth / White Cube
names.what: Mega-galleries with spaces in Hong Kong.

names.name: Leonardo da Vinci
names.what: His Salvator Mundi sold for $450 million in 2017, the auction record.

timeline.event: Picasso's Les Demoiselles d'Avignon launches Cubism.
Art HK fair launches; becomes Art Basel Hong Kong in 2013.
M+ opens; NFT art boom (Beeple sells for $69 million).
Christie's moves its Asia headquarters to The Henderson in Central.

now.headline: Market slowdown
now.detail: Auction sales fell from their 2022 peak, though top works still sell.

now.headline: Hong Kong's art week
now.detail: March's Art Basel week, with Art Central and gallery openings, is the city's art highlight.

now.headline: Immersive art
now.detail: Immersive exhibitions and digital art attract big crowds.

now.headline: Asian collectors
now.detail: Younger Asian collectors drive demand for contemporary artists.

local.headline: West Kowloon Cultural District
local.detail: M+, the Palace Museum, Xiqu Centre and harbourfront parks make it a great day out.

local.headline: Gallery districts
local.detail: H Queen's and Pedder Building in Central, plus Wong Chuk Hang's industrial galleries.

local.headline: Art Basel week
local.detail: Every March the city fills with collectors, parties and pop-up shows.

local.headline: Local artists
local.detail: Hong Kong artists like Samson Young, Shirley Tse and Angela Su have represented the city at the Venice Biennale.

debates.question: Is contemporary art a scam?
debates.sides: Some say prices are absurd; others value ideas over technique.

debates.question: Is art an investment?
debates.sides: A few works soar; most don't. Buy what you love.

debates.question: Are immersive shows real art?
debates.sides: Fun and accessible vs Instagram backdrops.
